reviewer: Cursor, pages opened via search, Australia/Brisbane
notice: General information, not legal advice. A 14-day line in a letter is the person's own deadline, not a statutory period. Statutory clocks below are only what the named official page said on the review date.

jurisdictions.name: Australia
jurisdictions.access_clock: Organisation: a reasonable period; OAIC thinks 30 days is reasonable. Agency: 30 days.
jurisdictions.complain_first: The organisation. Some sectors must use an external dispute scheme before the OAIC (energy, water, financial services, telecommunications, some transport, some tolls).
jurisdictions.regulator_name: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner
jurisdictions.regulator_when: No response within 30 days, or the response is unsatisfactory. Complaint must be in writing.

also_report.name: ReportCyber
also_report.note: Prefer this page. reportapp.cyber.gov.au returned a browser error on 15 Nov 2026. Phone 1300 292 371.

also_report.name: Scamwatch
also_report.note: Not a police report. Do not link a generic ACCC homepage for a lockout.

also_report.name: IDCARE
also_report.note: Support, not a regulator. 1800 595 160. Homepage on 15 Nov 2026 said a Microsoft Outlook outage was delaying email replies.

jurisdictions.name: New Zealand
jurisdictions.access_clock: Use the Privacy Commissioner's response-date calculator. Do not invent a day count in the Kit.
jurisdictions.complain_first: The agency. The Commissioner says a complaint that skipped this step will not be accepted.
jurisdictions.regulator_when: After the agency step. The Commissioner's page says an investigation queue of at least six months.

jurisdictions.name: United Kingdom
jurisdictions.access_clock: ICO: follow up if it has been over one month.
jurisdictions.complain_first: The organisation, as a data protection complaint.
jurisdictions.regulator_when: Within three months of the last meaningful contact with the organisation. ICO says it cannot represent the person and cannot award compensation.

also_report.name: Action Fraud
also_report.note: Fraud and cyber crime. 0300 123 2040. A data-breach report here is not automatically an ICO report.

jurisdictions.name: European Union
jurisdictions.access_clock: Do not hard-code a day count. The national authority's page governs.
jurisdictions.complain_first: The organisation, then the national data protection authority.
jurisdictions.regulator_name: National data protection authority (not the EDPB)
jurisdictions.regulator_when: The EDPB page sends the person to the authority where they live, work, or where it happened.

jurisdictions.name: United States
jurisdictions.access_right: No single federal access clock recorded in this pass
jurisdictions.access_clock: Do not invent one. State law differs.
jurisdictions.complain_first: The company, in the letter the Kit drafts.
jurisdictions.regulator_when: ReportFraud says it cannot resolve the individual report. It shares reports with law enforcers.

also_report.name: IdentityTheft.gov
also_report.note: Identity theft only. A knowingly false report is a crime under the page's own warning.

also_report.name: IC3
also_report.note: Cyber-enabled crime. IC3 warns that impersonators ask for money. Immediate danger: local emergency services, not this form.

jurisdictions.name: Canada
jurisdictions.access_right: PIPEDA s 4.9, as named in the RX
jurisdictions.access_clock: Not copied. The OPC access page was not opened in this pass.
jurisdictions.regulator_name: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada
jurisdictions.regulator_when: After the organisation. OPC says formal-complaint processing is delayed by several months.

also_report.name: Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre
also_report.note: Not confirmed on 15 Nov 2026. Do not invent a URL.
